clue.text: Reportedly, a gallon where cars stop for petrol?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the wordplay is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a gallon is four quarts in imperial measure

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls in to buy a gallon of fuel at a filling station.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecourt is the open paved area in front of a filling station where vehicles park at the pumps.

clue.text: Particular corporation after old odd-jobber

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming after means being placed below the earlier pieces, setting the order of the parts

parts.note: a particular is a detail or fact
O is the standard abbreviation for old
corporation is jocular slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A particular company takes on a man who used to do odd jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is old slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who does all sorts of work, a general handyman.

clue.text: 19 for restraint

parts.note: 19 is SAY CHEESE, so name a cheese out loud: the Greek feta

explanation.walkthrough: This is one of several clues where 19, SAY CHEESE, means: speak the name of a cheese. Spoken in a British accent, feta sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the ankles, and so any restraint.

clue.text: Tesla, say, on electronic charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing sitting on another is written above it, fixing the order of the two parts

parts.note: a Tesla is an example of a car
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A Tesla is plugged in to charge its electric battery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'charge' an electrical top-up; it is really responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone in your charge is to have them in your care: both mean custody or responsibility.

clue.text: Tough one overcoming evil, fragile thing?

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting on top of, so the first part is written above the second

parts.note: a teaser is a tough puzzle
vice is wickedness

explanation.surface: A tough person defeats evil, though they are rather fragile.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a set of cups, saucers and pots, usually china and easily broken; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Key dialect for slow mover

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
argot is the jargon or slang of a group

explanation.surface: An important regional speech used to describe a sluggish creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important, but it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: An escargot is a snail, especially one cooked to eat, and snails are proverbially sluggish.

clue.text: Mathematician touring Hanoi finally, a capital city

indicators.note: touring means travelling round something, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: John Venn, of Venn diagrams

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of Hanoi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mathematician on a tour of Vietnam visits its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanoi is itself a capital city, a decoy for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital of Austria.

clue.text: Certainly 19 with 23 down?

parts.note: 19 is SAY CHEESE; the cheese gruyere, spoken, is 23 down followed by this word

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a cheesy grin and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is GREW, and GREW plus the answer, spoken, gives the Swiss cheese gruyere.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is a casual form of yes, an affirmation like certainly.

clue.text: Figure holding publication on prayer — usually about that

indicators.note: something holding other things has them inside it

parts.note: one is a number, a figure

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: an Ave Maria is a prayer
a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A churchgoer usually reads a religious publication about prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means typically, as a rule, or roughly in that region.

clue.text: Show teeth, perhaps, first one extracted in a figure of speech

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, and first one picks the earlier of two letters i to go

parts.note: a simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another

explanation.surface: A dentist's image: teeth on display, the first one pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: The extraction suggests dentistry, but 'one' is the letter I, and the first of the two I's goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Smiling usually shows the teeth, so showing teeth is offered as an example of the action.

clue.text: Body cut, third of league qualify

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its end

parts.note: an entity is a body or being

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is two letters, here the opening third

parts.note: the first two of six letters, one third of the word

explanation.surface: A body's cut, and a third of the league fails to qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right to something, to qualify them for it.

clue.text: 25 stem
Animal, 19 with 22 down?

parts.note: 19 is SAY CHEESE; the cheese ricotta, spoken, is 22 down followed by this word

explanation.surface: A photographer asks an animal to grin for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is RICK, and RICK plus the answer, spoken, gives the Italian cheese ricotta.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating aquatic mammal, so a straightforward example of an animal.

clue.text: Some words, on leaving model, hit hard

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letters of the word on depart from the next word

parts.note: a paragon is a model of excellence
to rap is to strike
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A few words as someone departs: a model hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a section of writing made up of a group of sentences, some words.

clue.text: Disinfect food with a tissue, pre-cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Kitchen hygiene: wiping food with a tissue before cooking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pre-cooked' reads as one word, but splits into the last of the fodder and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteurising heats milk or other food to kill harmful microbes, which disinfects it.

clue.text: Very old house nearby, squalid

parts.note: handy means close at hand
squalid and nasty both mean foul

explanation.surface: An ancient house close by is in a filthy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' seems a building, but it means a royal family line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Han dynasty ruled China over two thousand years ago, and a dynasty is a ruling house.

clue.text: Wicked spinner with Kent is still upset by cut

parts.note: rump is a cut of beef

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A spin bowler for Kent is still upset at being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests cricket in the county of Kent, but it is the fairy-tale imp who spins straw into gold; 'by' puts the cut beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the malicious dwarf of the Grimm tale who spins straw into gold for a price.

clue.text: Gaps in fences regularly seen without reflection?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
holes are gaps

explanation.surface: Holes in fences appear without much thought being given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' does double duty: as outside, it puts the alternate letters around the gaps, and as lacking, it ends the definition. Reflection here is sound bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is reflected sound, so something echoless returns no reflection.

clue.text: Metric unit I record in score that's backed up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
backed up in a down clue means going upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a score in a test is a mark
a log is a record
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes a metric measurement in a score and backs it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass, a thousand grams.

clue.text: 10 from our gigolo only beginning to do this?

definitions.text: 10 from our gigolo only beginning to do this?

parts.note: surface: 10 is SMILE, and the clue asks what a photographer tells sitters to do to make them smile
setter's reading: say 'from our' and the first letter of gigolo, and it sounds like the French for cheese, fromage

explanation.surface: A photographer coaxes a smile from a reluctant gigolo.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'from our G' out loud gives fromage, so the instruction becomes literal: you are saying cheese, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask people to utter this phrase because it pulls the mouth into a grin.

clue.text: Unknown tag lifted, holding lead on springer spaniel

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised upwards, so the word reads bottom to top
holding means having something inside

parts.note: a tag is a name or label

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: An unidentified dog tag is lifted from a springer spaniel on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaniel' seems part of the dog's breed, but is the definition: a fawning follower.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniel is an old figurative word for a servile flatterer, just as a yes-man agrees with whatever a superior says.

clue.text: Nag, 19 with 4?

parts.note: 19 is SAY CHEESE; the Welsh cheese Caerphilly, spoken, is 4 down followed by this word

explanation.surface: A horse is coaxed into posing for a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is CARE, and CARE plus the answer, spoken, gives Caerphilly, a crumbly Welsh cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a horse, and a filly is a young female horse.

clue.text: Inlets where jay enters shallow waters

indicators.note: something entering goes inside another thing

parts.note: fords are shallow places for crossing a river
jay is the spelt-out name of the letter J

explanation.surface: Inlets where a bird enters the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jay' looks like the bird, but it is the name of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fjords are long narrow sea inlets between steep cliffs, as in Norway.

clue.text: Saint imprisoned by king, say, one taking stock

indicators.note: something imprisoned is shut inside its captor

parts.note: a king is an example of a ruler
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint jailed by a king takes stock of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking stock' suggests reviewing; stock here is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, and livestock is called stock.

clue.text: Wrench in heap?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to twist or sprain, as a joint
second meaning: a stack of hay or corn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrench' looks like a spanner, but means a sprain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a sprain such as a cricked neck, and also a stack of hay, as in hayrick.

clue.text: Birthplace of assassinated King, republic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Martin Luther King Jr was born in Atlanta, in this US state
second meaning: the country in the Caucasus

explanation.walkthrough: The capital K suggests a monarch, but the King is the civil rights leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the southern US state and to the former Soviet republic on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Rose coming up in flower garden

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means reading from bottom to top
in points to letters sitting inside the following words

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A rose pushing up in a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower, fitting the garden, but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose and grew are both past tenses meaning increased or went up.

clue.text: Polish collection

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a group or category of things

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes it look like the nationality, but it is polish as in sophistication.
explanation.definitionFit: Class means elegance or finesse, and also a set of things grouped together.

clue.text: True — 's very quick, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by the sound means the wordplay is matched to how it is spoken

parts.note: 's is S, very is dead (as in dead easy), quick is fast

explanation.surface: True, it is really quick, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means loyal and unwavering, as a true friend is.
